# KS-1033-item1 R16B-DEMOBASE - re-brief at develop 8c2f7b3fd of READY_KS-1033-item1_ornith35b-q4_BASHPATCH-RECOUNTED-PASS-7of7_2026-09-16.diff.md (written 2026-09-22 09:50:01 AEST by Wednesday's feed8 drafter; the product hunk and the new suite are the old READY's PASS 7/7 output re-anchored at the tip, every '+' line and every suite line made ASCII: the cell glyph is the word RED, em-dashes are hyphens; every context and '-' line asserted byte-exact at the tip at the line numbers below)

File: `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_demo_mutation_base.test.sh`
Tip: 8c2f7b3fd4fde915b2a24542bc32259b24e092a0
Runner: bash (the shell suite runner - `bash <file>` under /bin/bash 3.2; the checker runs the suite alone at the tip, then again after the script hunk)

## What is wrong (one paragraph)
`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh` refuses any change that touches a demo-shaping path
unless a commit in the range carries `[demo-mutation-allowed]`. It decides the range at `:51-60`: a
`GITHUB_BASE_REF` wins, then an explicit `$1`, and otherwise **it falls back to `BASE="origin/main"`
(`:58`)** and diffs `"$BASE...$HEAD"` (`:69`). The three-dot form takes the merge-base, which is right -
but the merge-base of `origin/main` and any develop-based branch is the point where `develop` was last
merged to `main`, **not** the branch point. Under Git Flow `develop` is permanently ahead of `main`, so
every develop-based branch is shown the whole develop-vs-main delta as if it were its own change. KS-1033
measured that on a branch that touched nothing: the guard reported four demo files as modified
(`deployment/azure/env.demo.json`, `migrate/Dockerfile`, `migrate/init.sql`, `migrate/run-platform.sh`).
This is not an abstract complaint - it is the sole reason the guard is UNWIRED. `run-code-guards.sh:116`
holds it in the `DEFERRED` bucket with exactly this reason and exactly this remedy in its own words:
*"Fix its base to the merge-base with origin/develop before wiring."* Until that is done the guard is a
check that cannot run, which is the defect KS-926 exists for; wired as-is it would demand
`[demo-mutation-allowed]` from every author on every push, which is the `--no-verify` generator KS-926
warns about. Changing the fallback to `origin/develop` makes `"$BASE...$HEAD"` resolve to the branch
point, so the diff contains the branch's own commits and nothing else.

**This is item 1 of KS-1033 and ONLY item 1.** The ticket records three unwired guards. Item 2
(`check-no-trust-header-reads.sh`, whose printed advice contradicts its own default) is explicitly
decision-class - the ticket says *"Deciding which is the point"* - and item 3
(`check-container-isolation.sh`) is a relocation to stack start-up, not an edit. Neither is touched here.
**Nothing in this task wires the guard**, either: it stays in `DEFERRED` and leg 15's census still
accounts for it, because wiring is a separate call that wants a measured push. This task removes the one
measured blocker the ticket names.

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-demo-mutation.sh - the DEFAULT diff
# base must be origin/develop, not origin/main (KS-1033 item 1)
# =============================================================================
# Under Git Flow develop is permanently ahead of main, so an origin/main base
# shows the whole develop-vs-main delta as this branch's own change. Every
# fixture is a throwaway repo under mktemp -d pushing to a LOCAL BARE REMOTE.
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/check_no_demo_mutation_base.test.sh
# =============================================================================

set -uo pipefail

export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SUBJ="${DEMO_GUARD_SH:-$HERE/../check-no-demo-mutation.sh}"
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: check-no-demo-mutation.sh not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks1033.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
PASS=0
FAIL=0
EXPECTED_CELLS=4
DEMO_FILE="Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/init.sql"
PLAIN_FILE="Blockchain/Dev/README.md"

build() {
  rm -rf "$1"
  mkdir -p "$1"
  (
    export GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null
    git init -q --bare -b main "$1/origin.git"
    git init -q -b main "$1/seed"
    cd "$1/seed" || exit 9
    git config user.email t@t.t
    git config user.name t
    mkdir -p Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate
    echo base > "$PLAIN_FILE"
    echo base > "$DEMO_FILE"
    git add -A
    git commit -qm init
    git checkout -q -b develop
    echo "develop moved ahead" > "$DEMO_FILE"
    git add -A
    git commit -qm "develop touches a demo path"
    git remote add origin "$1/origin.git"
    git push -q origin main develop
    cd "$1" || exit 9
    git clone -q "$1/origin.git" work
    cd "$1/work" || exit 9
    git config user.email t@t.t
    git config user.name t
    git checkout -q -b feature origin/develop
    if [ "$2" = demo ]; then
      echo "feature touches a demo path too" > "$DEMO_FILE"
    else
      echo "an ordinary change" > "$PLAIN_FILE"
    fi
    git add -A
    git commit -qm "feature work"
  ) > "$1/build.log" 2>&1
}

run_guard() {
  (
    unset GITHUB_BASE_REF
    if [ -n "$2" ]; then export GITHUB_BASE_REF="$2"; fi
    cd "$1/work" || exit 9
    bash "$SUBJ"
  ) > "$1/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}

build "$WORK/plain" plain
RC_PLAIN="$(run_guard "$WORK/plain" "")"
OUT_PLAIN="$WORK/plain/out.txt"
build "$WORK/demo" demo
RC_DEMO="$(run_guard "$WORK/demo" "")"
OUT_DEMO="$WORK/demo/out.txt"
build "$WORK/ciref" plain
RC_CIREF="$(run_guard "$WORK/ciref" develop)"
OUT_CIREF="$WORK/ciref/out.txt"

# CELL 1 (RED at the tip) - a develop-based branch that touched no demo path
# must be allowed. At the tip the origin/main base drags develop's own demo
# commit into the diff and the guard exits 1.
if [ "$RC_PLAIN" = "0" ]; then
  echo "PASS: a develop-based branch touching no demo path exits 0"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: a develop-based branch touching no demo path exited $RC_PLAIN, not 0 - the base dragged in develop's own commits ($(grep -c 'migrate/init.sql' "$OUT_PLAIN") demo path line(s) reported)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 2 (RED at the tip) - and it must say so, not print the block banner.
if grep -qF 'no demo-shaping paths touched' "$OUT_PLAIN" && ! grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_PLAIN"; then
  echo "PASS: the guard reports no demo-shaping paths touched and prints no block banner"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: clean-message present=$(grep -qF 'no demo-shaping paths touched' "$OUT_PLAIN" && echo yes || echo NO), block banner present=$(grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_PLAIN" && echo YES || echo no)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 3 (GREEN CONTROL, tip AND after) - the guard still refuses a REAL demo
# change on the branch itself. This is what stops a fix that just always passes.
if [ "$RC_DEMO" = "1" ] && grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_DEMO"; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL a branch that really touches a demo path is still blocked with exit 1"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL a real demo change exited $RC_DEMO (want 1), banner present=$(grep -qF 'DEMO MUTATION DETECTED' "$OUT_DEMO" && echo yes || echo NO)"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 4 (GREEN CONTROL, tip AND after) - GITHUB_BASE_REF still wins over the
# default, so the branch named there is what the diff is taken against.
if [ "$RC_CIREF" = "0" ] && grep -qF 'no demo-shaping paths touched' "$OUT_CIREF"; then
  echo "PASS: CONTROL GITHUB_BASE_REF=develop is still honoured ahead of the default"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: CONTROL GITHUB_BASE_REF=develop exited $RC_CIREF (want 0): $(head -1 "$OUT_CIREF")"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

# CELL 5 - the completeness guard. A suite that exits 0 having asserted nothing
# is a check that cannot fail, so a short count is itself a FAIL.
if [ $((PASS + FAIL)) -eq "$EXPECTED_CELLS" ]; then
  echo "PASS: all $EXPECTED_CELLS cells ran"; PASS=$((PASS+1))
else
  echo "FAIL: only $((PASS + FAIL)) of $EXPECTED_CELLS cells ran - a suite that asserts nothing is not a pass"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1))
fi

echo ""
echo "check_no_demo_mutation_base: $PASS passed, $FAIL failed"
[ $FAIL -eq 0 ]
```

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# DEMO-MUTATION GUARD (2026-04-28 demo-isolation lockdown)
# =============================================================================
# Refuses any commit that touches files known to shape the live demo
# environment, unless the commit message contains the explicit override
# token `[demo-mutation-allowed]`.
#
# Why this exists: the demo Azure environment (resource group
# secuura-demo-rg) is in active customer use during the connector-
# overhaul sprint. We disabled auto-deploy from main + develop in this
# commit, but a future engineer might re-enable it OR a config edit
# could shape the live env via secrets / Bicep templates without going
# through deploy. This guard is the second line of defence: PR review
# fails if the diff touches a demo-shaping path.
#
# Wired into:
#   - .github/workflows/ci.yml (build job, between lints and build)
#   - Pre-commit hook (optional, if developer wants local enforcement)
#
# To override (deliberate demo change):
#   git commit -m "Update demo config [demo-mutation-allowed]
#
#   Why: <explicit reason>"
#
# This is INTENTIONALLY noisy — false-positives are cheaper than
# accidentally shipping to live customers.
# =============================================================================

set -euo pipefail

# Paths that shape the live demo environment. Touching ANY of these
# requires the override token.
DEMO_PATHS=(
  "Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/env.demo.json"
  # NOTE (KS-318): the old Blockchain/Dev/.github/workflows/deploy-staging.yml
  # guard entry was dropped — that stale workflow dir was removed (GitHub only
  # runs the repo-root .github/workflows/). The live demo deploy is the
  # repo-root deploy-demo.yml; guarding it is a separate follow-up.
)

# Path PREFIXES that shape the demo environment. Anything under these
# trees is also gated.
DEMO_PREFIXES=(
  "Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/migrate/"
  # Bicep templates that drive the demo RG resources
)

# Determine the diff range. In CI this is the PR base..head; locally
# default to comparing against origin/main.
if [ -n "${GITHUB_BASE_REF:-}" ]; then
  BASE="origin/${GITHUB_BASE_REF}"
  HEAD="HEAD"
elif [ -n "${1:-}" ]; then
  BASE="$1"
  HEAD="${2:-HEAD}"
else
  BASE="origin/main"
  HEAD="HEAD"
fi

# Skip if we can't resolve the base (first commit on a fresh clone).
if ! git rev-parse --verify "$BASE" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "[demo-guard] base $BASE not found; nothing to compare"
  exit 0
fi

# Files changed in this diff
CHANGED_FILES=$(git diff --name-only "$BASE...$HEAD" 2>/dev/null || true)
if [ -z "$CHANGED_FILES" ]; then
  echo "[demo-guard] no files changed; nothing to check"
  exit 0
fi

# Find any demo-mutating change
MUTATIONS=()
while IFS= read -r f; do
  for p in "${DEMO_PATHS[@]}"; do
    if [ "$f" = "$p" ]; then
      MUTATIONS+=("$f")
      continue 2
    fi
  done
  for prefix in "${DEMO_PREFIXES[@]}"; do
    case "$f" in
      "$prefix"*) MUTATIONS+=("$f"); continue 2 ;;
    esac
  done
done <<< "$CHANGED_FILES"

if [ ${#MUTATIONS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
  echo "[demo-guard] no demo-shaping paths touched"
  exit 0
fi

# Demo path touched — check for the override token in any commit message
# in this diff range.
COMMIT_MSGS=$(git log "$BASE..$HEAD" --pretty=%B 2>/dev/null || true)
if echo "$COMMIT_MSGS" | grep -qF "[demo-mutation-allowed]"; then
  echo "[demo-guard] demo paths touched but override token present — allowed"
  echo "  paths:"
  printf '    %s\n' "${MUTATIONS[@]}"
  exit 0
fi

# No override → fail loudly
cat <<EOF >&2

╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║                  DEMO MUTATION DETECTED — BLOCKED                  ║
╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

This change touches files known to shape the live demo environment:

EOF

printf '    %s\n' "${MUTATIONS[@]}" >&2

cat <<EOF >&2

The live demo (Azure RG secuura-demo-rg) is in active customer use
during the connector-overhaul sprint. We don't want unintended config
shifts.

If this change is INTENTIONAL (deliberate demo update), add this
override token to ANY commit in the PR:

    [demo-mutation-allowed]

Example:
    git commit -m "Update demo env config [demo-mutation-allowed]

    Why: <explicit reason — what it does, who approved>"

If this change is unintentional, revert the demo-touching files
(or move them to a follow-up PR) and try again.

EOF

exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# TESTS for Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh — an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE
# (KS-877)
# =============================================================================
# The defect: with an empty SERVICES_TABLE, `docker-build.sh all` died at the
# banner's `${BUILD_LIST[*]}` with `BUILD_LIST[*]: unbound variable` under
# bash 3.2 + `set -u` — three lines after the `[ -n ]` guard added for exactly
# this class. That guard works (BUILD_LIST is left genuinely empty); the display
# expansion after it does not. And `${BUILD_LIST[*]:-}` alone only moves the
# death 55 lines down to the parallel loop's `"${BUILD_LIST[@]}"` — measured —
# so the shape that holds is a guard on `${#BUILD_LIST[@]}` that names the
# table and exits before either.
#
# docker is NEVER run: a stub on a private PATH records every call and exits 0,
# so the control cells can prove the working path still builds without a
# daemon. The empty table is produced by a fixture COPY of the subject whose
# heredoc body is stripped — the table is a literal inside the script, so
# there is no other way to reach the path — and the copy's row count is
# asserted 29 -> 0 before the cell is scored.
#
# Round 2 (KS-877, the tier-2 gate's F1): CELL 3 was RED on the repository's CI
# (ubuntu, bash 5.x) while green on macOS — `docker-build.sh`'s `((RUNNING++))`
# exits 1 when RUNNING is 0, and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` (COMPAT item 45) kills the
# script on it; bash 3.2 does not. CELL 4 pins the construct's ABSENCE statically
# (this box has no bash >= 4.1; CI's CELL 3 is the runtime instrument) and CELL 5
# proves the fix does not swallow a genuine build failure. The summary line
# carries the cell count (`(of N cells)`) and the run FAILS if fewer cells ran.
#
# Usage: bash Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/docker_build_empty_table.test.sh
#        DOCKER_BUILD_SH=/path/to/other/docker-build.sh bash …   (red-proof)
# =============================================================================
set -uo pipefail
TOTAL_CELLS=5

HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/../../../.." && pwd)"
# Same subject discipline as orchestrate_jobs.test.sh (KS-923 F2 / KS-941).
if [ "${DOCKER_BUILD_SH+set}" = set ] && [ -z "$DOCKER_BUILD_SH" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is set but EMPTY — refusing to silently grade the shipped script." >&2
  exit 2
fi
SUBJ="${DOCKER_BUILD_SH-$REPO_ROOT/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/docker-build.sh}"
[ -f "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: docker-build.sh not found at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
[ -r "$SUBJ" ] || { echo "FATAL: DOCKER_BUILD_SH is not readable at $SUBJ" >&2; exit 2; }
printf 'SUBJECT %s\n        sha256 %s\n\n' "$SUBJ" "$(shasum -a 256 "$SUBJ" | cut -d" " -f1)"

WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/ks877.XXXXXX")"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

pass=0; fail=0
ok()  { printf '  ok   %s\n' "$1"; pass=$((pass + 1)); }
bad() { printf '  FAIL %s\n     %s\n' "$1" "$2"; fail=$((fail + 1)); }

# Data rows of the SERVICES_TABLE heredoc in a script: tab-separated, not a
# comment. The same predicate service_names() applies.
table_rows() {
  sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$1" \
    | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/' | wc -l | tr -d ' '
}

# Build a fixture project root around a copy of the script under test.
#   $1 = dir   $2 = table: intact | emptied
# The copy lives at <root>/scripts/docker-build.sh so the script's own
# `PROJECT_ROOT="$SCRIPT_DIR/.."` resolves to the fixture root.
build_fixture() {
  local root="$1" table="$2"
  rm -rf "$root"; mkdir -p "$root/scripts" "$root/bin" "$root/services/auth"
  printf 'FROM scratch\n' > "$root/services/auth/Dockerfile"
  if [ "$table" = emptied ]; then
    # Strip every line between the heredoc's opening and closing markers.
    sed "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/{//!d;}" "$SUBJ" > "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  else
    cp "$SUBJ" "$root/scripts/docker-build.sh"
  fi
  # docker stub: records every call, succeeds.
  { printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\nexit 0\n' "$root"; } > "$root/bin/docker"
  chmod +x "$root/bin/docker"
}

# Run the copy with ONLY the stub dir in front of the system dirs. Prints rc.
run_build() {
  local root="$1"; shift
  ( export PATH="$root/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"; cd "$root" && bash scripts/docker-build.sh "$@" ) >"$root/out.txt" 2>&1
  echo $?
}
build_calls() { if [ -f "$1/docker_calls.txt" ]; then grep -c '^docker build' "$1/docker_calls.txt" || true; else echo 0; fi; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 1 — KS-877. THE REGRESSION. An EMPTY table must be refused by name —
# "no services matched", naming SERVICES_TABLE — with NO `unbound variable`
# and no build attempted. Asserted on rc = 1 AND the ABSENCE of the
# unbound-variable death AND the PRESENCE of the message naming SERVICES_TABLE
# AND 0 builds. rc alone cannot discriminate base from head (both exit 1),
# which is why the other three clauses exist; it is asserted so that a guard
# that prints the message and then exits 0 still reds (the gate's Tk). The row
# count is a precondition: a copy that still has rows would pass the pre-fix
# script and say nothing.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/empty" emptied
rows_subj="$(table_rows "$SUBJ")"; rows_copy="$(table_rows "$WORK/empty/scripts/docker-build.sh")"
if [ "$rows_subj" -lt 1 ] || [ "$rows_copy" -ne 0 ]; then
  bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
      "precondition broken: subject rows=$rows_subj (expected >=1), emptied copy rows=$rows_copy (expected 0) — the cell cannot discriminate"
else
  rc_empty="$(run_build "$WORK/empty" all)"
  if [ "$rc_empty" = 1 ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/empty")" -eq 0 ]; then
    ok "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE ($rows_subj rows -> $rows_copy) is refused by name — 'no services matched', naming SERVICES_TABLE — with no 'unbound variable', 0 builds, rc=$rc_empty"
  else
    bad "an EMPTY SERVICES_TABLE is refused by name with no 'unbound variable'" \
        "rc=$rc_empty, unbound variable present=$(grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo YES || echo no), message present=$(grep -q 'no services matched' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), table named=$(grep -q 'SERVICES_TABLE' "$WORK/empty/out.txt" && echo yes || echo NO), builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/empty"), last lines: $(tail -2 "$WORK/empty/out.txt" | sed 's|.*/scripts/||' | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 2 — CONTROL (the working path, one service). The intact table with
# `auth` must still print `Services:  auth`, build it once via the stub, report
# BUILD OK and exit 0. Without this, CELL 1 could pass by a guard that refuses
# every list.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/one" intact
rc_one="$(run_build "$WORK/one" auth)"
if [ "$rc_one" = 0 ] && grep -q '^  Services:  auth$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" && grep -q '\[auth\] BUILD OK' "$WORK/one/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/one")" -eq 1 ] && grep -q -- '-f services/auth/Dockerfile' "$WORK/one/docker_calls.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' prints 'Services:  auth', builds it once (-f services/auth/Dockerfile), BUILD OK, rc 0"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'auth' still builds it once and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_one, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/one"), output: $(grep -v '^=*$' "$WORK/one/out.txt" | tail -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 3 — CONTROL (the working path, every service, the parallel loop). The
# intact table with `all` must build every row via the stub and exit 0 — the
# path whose re-index guard (`${#PIDS[@]}`) the file's own comment documents,
# exercised under bash 3.2 with instant builds so the loop's empty-array case
# is actually reached.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/all" intact
rc_all="$(run_build "$WORK/all" all)"
if [ "$rc_all" = 0 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj):" "$WORK/all/out.txt" && grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/all/out.txt" \
   && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/all")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/all/out.txt"; then
  ok "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($rows_subj), rc 0, no unbound variable"
else
  bad "CONTROL — the intact table with 'all' builds every row and exits 0" \
      "rc=$rc_all, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/all") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED' "$WORK/all/out.txt" | head -3 | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 4 — KS-877 round 2 (the gate's F1). The subject has NO bare
# arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement (`((X++))` / `((X--))` on a line
# of its own). Such a command exits 1 when its expression evaluates to 0 — a
# post-increment yields the OLD value, so `((RUNNING++))` at RUNNING=0 "fails"
# — and bash >= 4.1 `set -e` exits on it (bash COMPAT item 45: "Bash-4.1 …
# exits when any command fails, not just a simple command or pipeline").
# bash 3.2 (macOS) does not, which is why CELL 3 was green here and RED on CI's
# ubuntu (run 34743050388: `rc=1, builds=0 of 29` — the script died after
# backgrounding ONE build). This is a STATIC pin, honest about being one: the
# runtime pin is CELL 3 on a bash >= 4.1, i.e. CI. The positive control inside
# the cell proves the grep can fire (a here-string holding `((X++))` -> 1).
# `[[:space:]]`, not `\s`: BSD grep.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
ARITH_RE='^[[:space:]]*\(\([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*(\+\+|--)\)\)[[:space:]]*$'
arith_control="$(printf '  ((X++))\n' | grep -cE "$ARITH_RE" || true)"
arith_hits="$(grep -nE "$ARITH_RE" "$SUBJ" || true)"
arith_count="$(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | grep -c . || true)"
if [ "$arith_control" != 1 ]; then
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "instrument cannot fire: the positive control read $arith_control (expected 1) — the cell is not scoring the subject"
elif [ "$arith_count" -eq 0 ]; then
  ok "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement — ((X++)) exits 1 at 0 and bash >= 4.1 set -e dies on it (control fires: $arith_control)"
else
  bad "the subject has NO bare arithmetic-command post-increment/decrement" \
      "count=$arith_count (control=$arith_control): $(printf '%s' "$arith_hits" | sed 's/^\([0-9]*\):[[:space:]]*/:\1 /' | tr '\n' ' ')"
fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# CELL 5 — KS-877 round 2, the MASK CONTROL. A run where ONE build genuinely
# fails must still land in `FAILED (1)` with rc 1 and the summary printed —
# the counter fix must not swallow a real failure. A second stub records the
# call, then exits 1 when its args name services/auth/Dockerfile (asserted
# unique among the table's rows). On bash 3.2 this reads the SAME before and
# after the fix — that IS the control: the fix changes nothing 3.2 can see
# except the arithmetic status; on CI (bash 5.x) it exercises the fixed loop
# under a genuine failure.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
build_fixture "$WORK/onefail" intact
{ printf '#!/bin/bash\n'; printf 'echo "docker $*" >> "%s/docker_calls.txt"\ncase "$*" in *services/auth/Dockerfile*) exit 1;; esac\nexit 0\n' "$WORK/onefail"; } > "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
chmod +x "$WORK/onefail/bin/docker"
auth_rows="$(sed -n "/^SERVICES_TABLE=\"\$(cat <<'SERVICES_EOF'\$/,/^SERVICES_EOF\$/p" "$WORK/onefail/scripts/docker-build.sh" \
  | awk -F'\t' 'NF==2 && $1 !~ /^[[:space:]]*#/ && $2 == "services/auth/Dockerfile"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
if [ "$auth_rows" -ne 1 ]; then
  bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
      "precondition broken: $auth_rows table rows resolve to services/auth/Dockerfile (expected exactly 1) — the failing stub cannot be aimed"
else
  rc_onefail="$(run_build "$WORK/onefail" all)"
  if [ "$rc_onefail" = 1 ] && grep -q "SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))):" "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && grep -q 'FAILED (1):' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && grep -q '^    auth$' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" && ! grep -q 'All builds succeeded' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" \
     && [ "$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail")" -eq "$rows_subj" ] && ! grep -q 'unbound variable' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt"; then
    ok "MASK CONTROL — with the auth stub exiting 1, 'all' still runs every row ($rows_subj stub builds), SUCCEEDED ($((rows_subj - 1))), FAILED (1): auth, rc 1"
  else
    bad "MASK CONTROL — one genuinely failing build still lands in FAILED (1), rc 1" \
        "rc=$rc_onefail, builds=$(build_calls "$WORK/onefail") of $rows_subj, output: $(grep -i 'unbound\|SUCCEEDED\|FAILED\|All builds' "$WORK/onefail/out.txt" | head -4 | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
fi

printf '\n  %d passed, %d failed (of %d cells)\n' "$pass" "$fail" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
# A cell that never ran is not a pass (KS-877 round 2): the ratio must add up.
if [ "$((pass + fail))" -ne "$TOTAL_CELLS" ]; then
  printf '  INCOMPLETE — %d of %d cells ran\n' "$((pass + fail))" "$TOTAL_CELLS"
  exit 1
fi
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ] || exit 1
exit 0
